newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Senate approves second section of budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian Senate approves second section of budget.

text.p: The upper house of parliament (Senate) on Wednesday approved the second section of the government's three-pronged 1997 budget.
The first section, which contained all the key budgetary measures for next year, has already been approved and parliamentary officials said voting on the final section would start later on Wednesday.

Earlier, Prime Minister Romano Prodi used a confidence vote to ram through part of the second section -- the 'finanziaria', which contains the overall spending plans for the various state bodies -- to sidestep a welter of opposition amendments.

The last part of the finanziaria was approved by a normal Senate vote. The centre-right opposition bloc boycotted the confidence vote, but some 40 politicians from the Freedom Alliance opposition returned to the upper house for the final ballot and managed to get some of their amendments approved.
Voting on the third section of the 1997 budget, which outlines spending plans for the various government ministries, was due to start at 1800 GMT.
A parliamentary official said he expected the vote to be concluded by the end of the day.

After the Senate has approved the budget, the package will return to the Lower House for a further reading. Ratification there is expected to be completed before Christmas. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
